title: Counting coins
examples: Teacher, how many coins make ten?
If I have a five and a one, what is the total?
Can we count these coins together?

explain.say: Today you will learn to count coins.
This coin is worth two. One coin can count as two.
This coin is worth five. Look at the number on the coin.
This coin is worth ten. It is worth the most of these coins.
Add the coins worth two and five. Start at five. Count on two: six, seven.

faq.q: How do I know which coin is which?
faq.a: The coins look different and have different numbers on them. You can look closely at the pictures.
asks: How can I tell them apart?

faq.q: If I have two five coins, is it ten?
faq.a: Yes, two five coins make ten units. You count five, then you count another five.
asks: Can two fives make a ten?

faq.q: Do I always count from the biggest coin first?
faq.a: It is easiest to count from the biggest coin to the smallest one. This helps you keep track.
asks: What is the best way to count?
Should I start with the ten coin?

faq.q: Is adding coins like adding toys?
faq.a: Yes, it is like counting toys. You put them together to see the total amount.
asks: Do I count them all together?

faq.q: What if I have a one, a two, and a five?
faq.a: Start with the five. Count on two: six, seven. Count on one more: eight. The total is eight.

facts: A one coin is worth one unit.
A two coin is worth two units.
A five coin is worth five units.
A ten coin is worth ten units.

quiz.say: Look at the coins. What are they worth altogether?
quiz.why: Start at five and count on two: six, seven.

wrong.0: Five is only the first coin, so count on two more.
wrong.2: Three is five take away two, but here you add.

quiz.say: Add the coins. How much are they worth?
quiz.why: Ten and one more make eleven.

wrong.1: Two is how many coins there are, but each coin has its own value.
wrong.2: Ten is only the big coin, so add the small coin too.

quiz.say: Count what the coins are worth. What is the total?
quiz.why: Five and five more make ten.

wrong.0: Five is one coin, so add the other five too.
wrong.1: Two is how many coins there are, and each one is worth five.
